forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Durham council implemented 97% of audit actions due by June; one Resources review rated limited
news_drafts.lead:
Durham County Council had carried out 392 of the 405 internal audit recommendations due by 30 June, or 97%, the Audit Committee was told at its meeting on 30 September. All 13 that missed their original dates have been given new ones, and none has missed the revised date.

The same quarterly report from Internal Audit, the team that checks the council's controls, records one review in the quarter with a limited assurance opinion, meaning controls were not reliably managing the risks identified. It was in the Resources service grouping, and the detail is in a confidential Part B paper. Unplanned staff absences meant the team delivered 723 productive days, 18% of the annual plan against the 22.5% expected for the quarter. The report says the service was back to full staffing by the start of the second quarter. A review of the Digital Durham Grant was dropped from the plan because there was no spend on the programme this year. The paper gives no reason.

The committee's annual report sets out the wider record. Forvis Mazars, the external auditor, gave an unqualified opinion (full sign-off) on the 2024/25 accounts and on the council's value for money arrangements on 26 November 2025. Internal Audit's overall opinion on the control environment for 2025/26 was "moderate". On 31 July the Corporate Director of Resources concluded the council has "a history of stable finance" and no significant risks to its continuing operation. A Local Government Association peer review in October 2025 called it "a financially well-managed and stable organisation", with debt and reserves "consistent with accepted sector practice".

The committee also heard from the Corporate Director of Children and Young People's Services on 27 February about rising Children in Care costs, including unregulated and crisis placements. On 26 March it held a special meeting on the governance, decision-making and value for money of the Toft Hill and High Etherley Bypass, focused on what lessons can be taken forward.

news_drafts.headline: County Durham faces £83.7m four-year budget deficit from 2027/28, £38.9m worse than last year's forecast
news_drafts.lead: County Durham faces a four-year budget deficit of £83.7 million over 2027/28 to 2030/31, £38.9 million worse than forecast last year. Planned savings of £21.5 million leave a £62.1 million gap, requiring either higher council tax or service cuts. The immediate crisis lies in 2027/28 and 2028/29, when the cumulative cash shortfall of £49.7 million will exceed the council's reserves (money set aside) of £34.6 million. The council warns that such over-reliance on reserves has forced other councils into Exceptional Financial Support, a government regime that removes local control of spending—36 councils faced this in 2026/27, up from 29 the year before. Adult social care costs heighten the pressure: £34.4 million in fee uplifts over four years against only £25.9 million raised by the dedicated precept, the extra council tax for this service.

findings.headline: Council detected and prevented approximately £1.133 million in fraud, overpayments and error during 2025/26.
findings.detail: Corporate Fraud Team received 1,117 referrals and retained 709 cases for investigation. Fraud identified/prevented comprised £505,380 from direct corporate fraud and £627,590 from housing fraud via partner arrangements. Highest-volume areas were Council Tax Fraud (513 referrals) and Council Tax Reduction Scheme fraud (332 referrals). Team delivered 38 prosecutions and sanctions. Management confirms no material impact on statement of accounts.
findings.matters: Demonstrates active and effective fraud detection capability protecting council assets. High referral volume reflects high-fraud-risk environment (benefits, discounts, taxes) but effective controls with significant recoveries indicate strong financial safeguards.
findings.figures: £1.133m identified/prevented (£505,380 corporate; £627,590 housing); 1,117 referrals; 709 cases retained (63%); 38 prosecutions and sanctions
findings.quote: The Team identified or prevented fraud, overpayments and error valued at approximately £1.133 million, comprising £505,380 from direct corporate fraud investigations and a further £627,590 from housing-related fraud investigations undertaken through partnership arrangements with Registered Social Landlords.

findings.headline: External LGA peer review found council is financially stable and well-managed with reserves at accepted sector levels.
findings.detail: October 2025 Local Government Association peer review concluded Durham County Council is 'financially stable organisation with strong, unified culture' delivering 'high-performing services and outcomes relative to the rest of the sector.' Financial management section found council 'financially well-managed' with 'levels of debt and reserves consistent with accepted sector practice, and it consistently produces timely accounts.'
findings.matters: Independent external validation by LGA provides credible assessment of council's financial management quality relative to sector peers, relevant to lenders evaluating creditworthiness and financial stability.
findings.quote: Durham County Council is a financially well-managed and stable organisation. Its levels of debt and reserves are consistent with accepted sector practice, and it consistently produces timely accounts.

findings.headline: No events identified that would cast doubt on the council's ability to continue as a going concern.
findings.detail: Audit Committee confirmed on 31 July 2026 that going concern basis is appropriate for the financial statements. No events or conditions identified since then that would create doubt about the council's ability to operate and discharge liabilities over the next 12+ months.
findings.matters: Going concern status is fundamental to lenders' assessment of a council's financial viability and ability to service debt over the medium term.
findings.figures: Assessment period to 31 March 2026; forward-looking period of at least 12 months
findings.quote: It did not identify any event that would cast a significant doubt on the organisation's ability to continue as a going concern.

findings.paper_title: 06 Annual Report of the Audit Committee for the period September 25 to August 26
findings.headline: Special Audit Committee meeting on 26 March 2026 examined the Toft Hill and High Etherley Bypass scheme's governance, decision-making and value for money, with focus on lessons learned.
findings.detail: A dedicated audit committee meeting was convened to review this capital project, specifically examining governance and value-for-money aspects, with focus on understanding what was known at the time, how decisions were made, and what lessons could be taken forward. The fact that this project warranted a special audit review suggests governance or value-for-money considerations merited specific scrutiny.
findings.matters: Special audit scrutiny of a capital project indicates it merited close examination of governance and value-for-money execution, which would concern a lender assessing the council's project delivery and capital management.
findings.quote: The Committee received a presentation of the Corporate Director of Neighbourhoods and Environment which presented the details of the development of the Toft Hill and High Etherley Bypass scheme considering the governance, decision-making and value of money in relation to the project, with a focus on understanding what was known at the time, how decisions were made, and what lessons could be taken forward.

findings.paper_title: 06 Annual Report of the Audit Committee for the period September 25 to August 26
findings.headline: Children in Care cost pressures are driving increasing financial pressures that the Council is actively managing and seeking to mitigate.
findings.detail: The Audit Committee specifically requested a presentation on 27 February 2026 from the Corporate Director of Children and Young People's Services to understand factors driving increasing cost pressures in Children in Care. The presentation covered the use of unregulated and crisis placements and the arrangements and controls in place over such placements, indicating this is an active area of financial and operational risk management.
findings.matters: Material cost pressures in children's services are a key financial sustainability issue for councils and directly relevant to a lender's assessment of financial position and budget management capability.
findings.quote: A presentation by the Corporate Director of Children and Young People's Services which provided an overview of the factors driving the increasing cost pressures associated with Children in Care and the action the Council was taking to manage and mitigate those cost pressures, as requested by the Audit Committee.
